DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE AT VIJAYAPUR IN  CRL.A.NO.5/2016 FOR THE OFFENCE PUNISHABLE UNDER  SECTIONS 7(1), 16(1)(A) AND (B) OF PREVENTION OF FOOD  ADULTERATION ACT OR ALTERNATIVELY REMAND THE CASE  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-K:6506  CRL.RP No. 200076 of 2018 TO THE TRIAL COURT FOR FRESH DISPOSAL IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW,
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE K NATARAJAN  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE K NATARAJAN) This revision petition is filed by the petitioner-accused under section 397 of Cr.P.C. for setting aside the order passed by the III Additional District and Sessions Judge at Vijayapur in Criminal Appeal No.5/2016 dated 16.10.2018 for having allowed the appeal filed by the State under Section 377 of Cr.P.C. for the offences punishable under Sections 7(1), 16(1)(A) and (B) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (hereinafter referred to as 'PFA Act').
2. Heard the Learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent State.
3.
The case of prosecution is that the Kirana shop of the petitioner was said to be raided by the authorities, where they came to know that the petitioner had stored adulterated salt.
Accordingly, the charge sheet was filed before the JMFC, Bagewadi for the offences punishable under Sections 7(1), 16(1)(A) and (B) of the PFA Act.
The petitioner appeared before the Magistrate and pleaded guilty.
Accordingly, the learned Magistrate sentenced the petitioner to pay a fine of Rs.6,000/- and there is no order passed for a minimum sentence under the PFA Act.
Therefore, the State preferred an appeal under section 377 of Cr.P.C. for the inadequate sentence passed by the trial Court.

Accordingly, the appeal came to be allowed by the Sessions Judge, and petitioner was convicted and sentenced to undergo the imprisonment for 3 months as per section 16(1) of the PFA Act vide order dated 16.10.2018, which is under challenge.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the first appellate Court has committed error in enhancing the sentence, even though the petitioner pleaded guilty.

sentences.text: rightly passed the sentence of Rs.6,000/- as fine, that is sufficient.
The petitioner was found only with adulterated salt, which is not more cost.
Therefore, prayed for allowing the in the petition .
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader contended that as per the law, minimum 6 months imprisonment shall be imposed other than the fine amount.
But, the first applied Court has awarded only 3 months imprisonment, which is sufficient and therefore, prayed for dismissing the petition.
6. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties, perused the records.
7. It is not in dispute that the petitioner pleaded guilty and he has been convicted for the offence is punishable under Sections 7(1), 16(1)(A) and (B) of the PFA Act.
The trial Court imposed the fine of Rs.6,000/- without any sentence of imprisonment.
Hence, the State filed an appeal.
As per section 16 of the PFA Act, the minimum punishment prescribed is not less than six months, which can be extended up to 3 years.

It is further provided that the Court, may by adequate and special reasons,
impose lesser punishment but shall not less than 3 NC: 2024:KHC-K:6506 months and it may extend to 2 years and fine and the fine shall not be less than Rs.500/-.
8.

The first appellate Court has also relied upon the judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of STATE THROUGH INTELLIGENCE OFFICER NARCOTIC CONTROL BUREAU Vs.
MUSTAK AHMED ETC. reported in 2015(4) Crimes 143 (SC), where the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that when the law mandates the minimum sentence, the Court has no power to reduce the same by granting any lesser sentence.

entities.text:
STATE THROUGH INTELLIGENCE OFFICER NARCOTIC CONTROL BUREAU Vs.
MUSTAK AHMED ETC. reported in 2015(4) Crimes 143 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the minimum sentence prescribed under section 16 of the PFA Act is 6 months which extended up to 3 years, but by giving the adequate reasons, the Court can reduce the sentence of imprisonment minimum of 3 months.

The petitioner himself has pleaded guilty, therefore, I am of the view that the minimum sentence of imprisonment of 3 months awarded by the first appellate Court is sufficient and the same cannot be reduced and the said sentence passed by the first appellate Court does not call for any interference.
9.

Accordingly, I pass the following order:
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6506 (i) The revision petition by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.
(ii) Office is directed to send the copy of this order to the trial Court.
(iii) The petitioner shall surrender before the trial Court.
